root_cause.text: `persistent_ram_save_old()` in `fs/pstore/ram_core.c` reused `prz->old_log` across calls without checking whether the persistent RAM buffer size had changed, so it could copy a larger `size` into an older, smaller `old_log` and leave `old_log_size` inconsistent, causing heap out-of-bounds access in `memcpy_fromio()` and later reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (prz->old_log && prz->old_log_size != size) persistent_ram_free_old(prz);` before allocating, and the CVE description says the function “only allocates prz->old_log when it is NULL, but it unconditionally updates prz->old_log_size to the current buffer size and then performs memcpy_fromio() using this new size,” which leads to OOB write/read when the buffer grew between calls.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free and reallocate persistent old_log storage when the saved crash size changes to avoid size-mismatch reuse.
intent_record.what: In persistent_ram_save_old(), a new comment and a conditional were added before allocating old_log: if prz->old_log already exists and its recorded size differs from the current size, persistent_ram_free_old(prz) is called to free the old buffer so a new one can be allocated.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures a stale old_log buffer from a previous save is discarded when the expected dump size changes, preventing reuse of a buffer with the wrong size and allowing the function to reallocate storage that matches the current crash data.

grouping_result.intent: Free and reallocate persistent old_log storage when the saved crash size changes to avoid size-mismatch reuse.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents reuse of an old_log buffer when the persistent RAM size changes, which addresses the size mismatch that led to out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This line allocates old_log only when it is initially NULL, but the pre-fix logic reused the same buffer on later calls even if the crash record size changed. That size-mismatch reuse is the root cause of the out-of-bounds copy/read.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation is only performed when old_log is NULL in the pre-fix code, so later calls reused an existing buffer even if the persistent RAM size changed. That allowed a larger size to be copied into a stale, smaller old_log, leading to out-of-bounds access and inconsistent old_log_size.
